description:
About the Position

Utrecht University is hiring an Impact and Stakeholder Coordinator to strengthen the connection between its research and the partners who use it. The role coordinates impact activities across projects and faculties: building stakeholder relationships, organising knowledge exchange and supporting researchers in planning, monitoring and reporting the societal impact of their work.

The coordinator works with academic staff, external partners and the university's research-support services. Day-to-day tasks include mapping stakeholder networks, facilitating workshops and co-creation sessions, advising on impact strategies for funding proposals, and maintaining the university's impact monitoring practices. It is a professional staff appointment under the university's employment conditions.

Candidate Profile

Applicants have a relevant master's-level background and experience in research support, knowledge transfer, science communication or stakeholder management in an academic environment. Strong organisational and communication skills in English are essential; Dutch is an advantage for national stakeholder work. The position is a salaried staff role on the Utrecht University employment scale, with a fixed closing date for applications.

Highlights

  • Research impact coordination and monitoring
  • Stakeholder network building and facilitation
  • Knowledge exchange and co-creation workshops
  • Support for impact strategies in funding proposals
  • Cross-faculty collaboration with research groups
  • Professional staff appointment at Utrecht University

About Utrecht University

Utrecht University is a leading Dutch research university, consistently ranked among the top institutions in Europe. Its research and teaching span four faculties and a broad range of strategic themes, including sustainability, dynamics of youth, institutions for open societies and life sciences. PhD candidates and postdocs in the Netherlands are salaried staff members with full employment benefits under the CAO-NU collective agreement, so advertised positions are fully funded. Academic and support vacancies are published on the university's working-at portal, with clear deadlines and application instructions per position.
